summary: Mark A. Nathan works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD from UCLA (2010), supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held posts at UCLA, Kangwon National University, and the University at Buffalo.

Mark Allon is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctorate at the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman (~1989-1994). He served as an Associate Professor at the University of Sydney (2002).

Mark Collins, an Indologist and linguist, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (1905-1907). He served as Professor of English at Banaras Hindu University (1900-1904) and Professor of Sanskritic Philology at the University of Madras (1914-1919).
Mark Condos is a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge (2009-2013). He has held posts at Queen Mary University of London (2014) and King's College London (2020).

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He served as an Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994-2007) and became a Professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 2010.

Mark D. Griffiths earned his PhD from the University of Exeter (1988-1990). He held a lectureship at the University of Plymouth (1990-1995) and served as Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995-2025).

Mark Elliott is a historian specializing in sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a professor of history at UC Santa Barbara (~1993-2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University (~2003).
Mark Hale is a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He has held attested positions at Harvard University (1987) and Concordia University (1997).

Mark I. Wallace specializes in religious studies and philosophy, completing his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul Ricœur (~1982-1986). He taught at Georgia State University (~1987-1989) before becoming Professor of Religion at Swarthmore College (~1989).

Mark Jan Dresden worked in Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1937-1941) and served as Professor of Iranian Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (1949-1980).
Mark Juergensmeyer is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (1967-1974). He held posts at UC Santa Barbara (1993) and Claremont McKenna College.

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held faculty posts at the University at Albany, SUNY, and serves as Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair in Japanese Studies at UC Berkeley.
Mark McClish is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who was a doctoral student of Patrick Olivelle. His academic affiliations include a post at Birmingham-Southern College (attested 2012).
Mark Owen is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral research under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Mark Pedersen is a computational linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Queensland (-2001) and later held an academic post there.
Mark Rowe is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He holds a post as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at McMaster University.

Indologist Mark S. G. Dyczkowski studied at Banaras Hindu University (1970-1974) and earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson (~1974-1979), later receiving a DLitt from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1985).

Mark Siderits is a philosopher working in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Illinois State University (~1979-2008) and later at Seoul National University (~2008-2012).

Mark Singleton, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, completed his M.Phil (1997-1998) and PhD (2003-2006) at the University of Cambridge. He held a professorship at St John's College (2007-2013) and a senior research fellowship at SOAS (2015).

Mark T. Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1977-1981) and Stanford University (~1988-1994), holding posts at Brown University and the University of Oregon (~2000).
